question: Fulfilment of milestone 87 of Spain’s Recovery, Transformation and Resilience Plan (RTRP) and the true state of rail safety upgrades on the Madrid-Seville line

Spain notified the Commission that it had fulfilled milestone 87 of the RTRP, covering the implementation of contracts across 1 400 km of the TEN-T core network. However, the fatal accident in Urda occurred when the ERTMS planned for the MadridSeville line, whose deployment is part of the EU-funded modernisation programme, was reportedly not yet fully operational.

This raises questions as to whether the implementation reported by the Spanish Government to the Commission accurately reflected the true state of the upgrades intended to strengthen safety on the line. 1.

Can the Commission specify which contracts, and which specific contract sections for the Madrid-Seville corridor, were submitted by Spain as evidence of having met milestone 87, and what specific documentation is it examining to verify that implementation?

Did the documentation merely certify the contractual completion of the works, or did it also prove that the equipment – particularly the ERTMS system – had been installed, tested, validated and put into active service?

If it were found that a safety measure declared as completed was not physically operational on the certified date, would the Commission review whether milestone 87 was actually fulfilled and determine whether that discrepancy could have affected the safety risk assessment for the line?
